title: Smoothness of the Gaussian Fourier integral
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $a\in\mathbb R$, and let $H:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb C$ be strongly measurable almost everywhere with respect to standard Gaussian measure $\gamma$ on $\mathbb R^n$. Suppose there is a real constant $C$ such that $\|H(t)\|\le C$ for every $t\in\mathbb R^n$. Then the function of $x\in\mathbb R^n$ given by $\int_{\mathbb R^n}\exp\!\left(i a\sum_{j=1}^n t_jx_j\right)H(t)\,d\gamma(t)$ is infinitely continuously differentiable.
